page.layout: One column of running text, with a black-letter German verse couplet set inside it. Below the last line, at the right, a catchword. No margin notes.

main_text.p: eft, ne turpitudinis gratia affectatum, & cū ejusdem religionis viro contractum. Quæ enim pars fideli cum infideli[?] 2. Corinth. 6.

Nonnulli tamen latius patere judicant, nempe ut religiosè & cum timore Domini id faciant, & secundum ejus præscriptum in nomine Domini Iesu, Colos. 3. in gloriam Dei, 1. Corinth. 10. non extra Dominum aut contra Dominum, sed consulto Domino & invocato nomine ejus. Sic enim auspicato matrimonia contrahuntur. Non igitur moveantur ut equus & mulus effrænata libidine, sed adsit verecundia & modestia Christianis digna. Nam qui Deum à se & à sua mente excludunt, super eos dæmon habet potestatem, Tob. 6. Et quoniam matrimonium est non solùm legitima, seu licita ex ordine & instituto Dei, sed etiam perpetua ac insolubilis, duorum maris scilicet & fœminæ, studio gignendæ sobolis, & vitandæ fornicationis, conjunctio seu copulatio in carnem unam: non temerè & absque consilio ac deliberatione ineundum est. Quoniam, ut habet Mimus Publianus: Deliberandum est diu, quod statuendum est semel:

p.bl: Dann vorgethan/und erst darnach betracht/ Hat manchen in groß leiden gebracht.

main_text.p: ȝ[?] Tertiò ostendit Paulus, utrum melius & commodius sit in viduitate permanere, vel iterum matrimonium contrahere. Felicior est, inquit, (non coram Deo, sed in hac vita, id est, non sanctior erit, sed commodius ha-

page.notes: Long s normalised to s; u/v and i/j spelling changed as rule requires. The black-letter couplet was copied letter by letter from Fraktur; "vnd" was read as "und" by the u/v rule. Doubtful: the mark after "infideli" (read as a question mark, possibly a printed sign) and the paragraph mark before "Tertiò" (read as ȝ). "Publianus" is read from a worn word. The scan is cut off at the right edge of the text block, and the line "sed commodius ha-" continues on the next page.
